question: Can decision-time observations predict expected residual initial-proposal shares beyond zero and train-mean controls?
label: Exact absolute acquired-share difference between the two initial proposal legs; post-execution label only.
primary_metric: Equal-base-group validation RMSE; also retain aggregate MAE/RMSE and positive-outcome errors.
selection_rule: Compare mean neural episode RMSE across two optimizer seeds with deterministic ridge; prefer ridge unless neural mean improves by at least 0.10 shares. This is a declared practical tolerance, not established statistical significance.
final_test: Not opened in these training jobs.
policy_integration: None: shares predictions are excluded from probability gates; no change to existing policies.
limitations: Zero-heavy labels can favor underprediction; positive errors and zero/train-mean controls must accompany aggregate metrics.
Optimizer seeds reuse the same data and are not independent market observations.
Synthetic fills, initial-admission scope only; no dollar loss or empirical fill calibration.

optimizer_configuration.neural: AdamW lr=0.001, betas=(0.9,0.999), eps=1e-8, weight_decay=0.01, amsgrad=False
optimizer_configuration.ridge: alpha=1; squared shares loss plus L2 penalty; output clipped nonnegative
